pathway.title: GRAY MEDIA, INC — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is high on both reported and adjusted earnings. Net debt over reported EBITDA was 4.90x at FY2024, 8.55x at FY2025 and 8.42x on the last twelve months, and 7.94x on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, because reported EBITDA fell 43.84% as political advertising fell 91.55%, so creditors carry the debt on off-year earnings until 2026 political revenue is booked. The pro forma figure after the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment is USD 5,675 million, or 8.48x; the figure after the 2026-07-21 repurchase is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11

Interest cover is the thinnest dimension. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.84x at FY2024, 1.60x at FY2025 and 1.74x on the last twelve months, and adjusted EBITDA covered it 1.84x, so a repeat of the off-year trough would leave little room for a cost or revenue miss. Cash interest takes 12.23% of last-twelve-months revenue. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12

Free cash flow is positive but small relative to the debt. Operating cash flow of USD 250 million less capital spending of USD 104 million gave USD 146 million over the last twelve months, and after USD 87 million of common and preferred dividends only USD 59 million remained, so deleveraging from internal cash flow is slow unless earnings rise. The FY2025 off-year left USD 96 million after the same items. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C9

The maturity profile is the main support. No principal falls due before 2028, the USD 739 million term loan and the USD 750 million revolver are both due on 2028-12-01, and the USD 1,125 million of 2029 first lien notes follow, so USD 1,864 million, or 31.77% of principal, comes due by the end of 2029. Secured debt is 65.78% of principal, so the unsecured notes of USD 2,008 million rank behind a large secured layer. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 37

Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was USD 921 million, made of cash and revolver availability, before the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment and the July 2026 repurchase funded partly from the revolver, so cash after those events is not established. The receivables securitization of USD 400 million is fully drawn, so it adds no further funding, and the revolver amount drawn is not stated, so liquidity today is not established. Basis: calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 25, 33–34; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5

Revenue durability depends on fee contracts and the election cycle. Retransmission consent and network affiliation economics set the cash margin, and political advertising swings earnings between even and odd years, so the 2027 off-year and the renewals of network agreements from mid-2027 to the end of 2028 are the periods in which refinancing and earnings pressures meet. Management guidance for the third quarter of 2026 points to revenue of USD 935 million to USD 965 million against USD 749 million a year earlier, which is guidance and not an outcome. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5

Governance and financial policy are mixed and add to the balance sheet risk. The earlier assessment rates sponsor and governance risk as medium because acquisitions were funded partly with first lien notes while dividends continued, and because a ten-vote share class concentrates voting power; the preferred stock repurchase at a discount and the debt repurchases are the countervailing actions. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: Scale and market rank are a strength. The group reaches about 37% of US households and holds the top-rated station in 77 markets, with no market above 5% of revenue, so a local downturn or one lost advertiser does little to debt service and the stations keep bargaining power with distributors, which supports refinancing access. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 4

A back-ended maturity profile is a strength. No principal is due before 2028 and USD 1,864 million falls due by the end of 2029, so the company does not need the capital markets in the 2026 cycle, which lowers near-term default risk even though leverage is high. Basis: calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 16

A path to higher earnings in the current cycle is a strength. Political advertising of USD 113 million in the first half of 2026 and guided third quarter political revenue of USD 165 million to USD 185 million would lift twelve-month earnings and cover if realised, which gives management a credible route to deleveraging without asset sales. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5

Leverage and cover on reported earnings are the main weakness. Net debt of 8.42x reported EBITDA (8.48x pro forma after the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment) and cover of 1.74x leave little tolerance for a miss, so a fall in earnings would raise leverage and squeeze free cash flow before any covenant is tested. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)

Dependence on fee contracts and the cycle is a weakness. Retransmission consent revenue was 46.17% of FY2025 revenue and network fees took a large share of it, with political advertising 1.36% of revenue in the off-year, so earnings can fall by 43.84% between an election year and the following year and renewals can reset fees. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C15; calculation C16

Policy and secured-debt priority are a weakness. Acquisitions funded partly with first lien notes and maintained dividends raise secured debt ahead of the unsecured and second lien notes, and the family-influenced control structure means these choices are decided by shareholders, so recovery for junior creditors is more exposed. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: In the first half of 2026 the company closed station purchases with stated consideration of USD 280 million: WBBJ USD 27 million, three Allen Media stations USD 56 million, seven Allen Media markets USD 115 million, Block Communications stations USD 80 million and Sagamore Hill stations USD 2 million. It also swapped three stations to Scripps for two others without cash, recording a non-cash loss of USD 22 million. Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13

On 2026-06-30 the company issued USD 70 million of additional 7.25% first lien notes due 2033 at par in a private placement. The proceeds paid USD 40 million of the first closing of the American Spirit Media acquisition and USD 30 million to repurchase 50,000 Series A preferred shares with USD 50 million of liquidation preference. On 2026-07-01 the first closing of American Spirit Media and WHPM was paid in cash, and USD 11 million remains payable at the second closings, which need regulatory approval. Basis: calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 18, 25; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5

In 2025 the company refinanced most debt: USD 900 million and USD 250 million of 9.625% second lien notes due 2032, USD 775 million of 7.25% first lien notes due 2033, and a revolving credit facility raised to USD 750 million and extended to 2028-12-01. The proceeds redeemed the 2027 notes at par, repaid term loans and redeemed part of the 2029 first lien notes at 103% of par. Later in 2026 the company repurchased USD 100 million of 2029 first lien notes and USD 20 million of 2031 notes at par. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 92–94; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: GRAY MEDIA, INC (issuer id gtn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, ownership, governance, financial policy and transaction facts that matter to a creditor, from the annual report, the latest quarterly report and two earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gray Media is a sturdy station operator whose scale and market positions support creditors, but family-influenced control, a ten-vote share class and debt-funded station purchases beside maintained dividends make sponsor and governance risk medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors rely on management policy rather than documented limits, because the debt agreements and the proxy statement were not supplied. The risk would rise if acquisitions keep being funded with secured debt while dividends continue, and would fall with documented debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating business is the credit's strength: the stations are well diversified, with the largest market at 5% of revenue and the ten largest markets at about 25%, and most markets are led by a first or second ranked station. That breadth lowers the chance that one local market or one advertiser damages debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Half of revenue is now fee income negotiated with distributors and networks rather than advertising, which makes renewals the main business risk. Retransmission consent revenue was 46.17% of FY2025 revenue and network affiliation fees took 28.50% of it, so net retransmission revenue of USD 547 million depends on subscriber trends and on affiliation agreements that expire from mid-2027 to the end of 2028, the same window in which the 2028 term loan and revolver mature.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings swing with the election cycle, so a single year says little about debt service. Political advertising was USD 497 million, or 13.64% of revenue, in FY2024 and USD 42 million, or 1.36%, in FY2025, so creditors should read leverage across the full two-year cycle and not on an election year alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Voting control sits with the Class A holders and the Howell-Robinson Family, whose stake is not established. Each Class A share carries ten votes, which gives that class 51.45% of votes on the share counts at 2026-07-31, and the filing states that the Howell-Robinson Family can exert significant influence over policies and management. Creditors therefore face shareholder decisions on acquisitions, dividends and leverage that are not checked by an outside controlling holder, and a change of control would trigger mandatory redemption of the USD 600 million Series A preferred stock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is mixed: growth is funded partly with secured debt while shareholders are paid. The company bought stations for USD 280 million of stated consideration in the first half of 2026, issued USD 70 million of first lien notes to fund the American Spirit Media closing and a preferred stock repurchase, and paid common dividends of USD 33 million and preferred dividends of USD 52 million in FY2025. The preferred repurchase paid USD 30 million for USD 50 million of liquidation preference, which cut junior claims and the cash dividend by USD 4 million a year, but the new first lien debt ranks ahead of the unsecured and second lien notes.

fields.value: Reporting quality supports monitoring. The auditor has served since 2006, disclosure controls were found effective at year end, and the quarterly report and earnings release print the covenant leverage calculation in full, so creditors can follow covenant ratios each quarter even though the debt documents were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Licence dependence and regulation tie the asset value to the FCC. Broadcast licences and goodwill were 78.15% of total assets at 2026-06-30, the national ownership limit of 39% of households (with a discount for UHF stations) caps further scale, and the second closings of the latest acquisitions await regulatory approval, so deal-funded growth depends on rule changes that management expects but the filings do not guarantee.

fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a lower risk reading is the operating record and the preference for reducing junior claims: the preferred repurchase was done at a 40.00% discount to liquidation preference, the board authorized up to USD 250 million of debt repurchases through 2027, and the company repurchased USD 120 million of notes at par in July 2026. The view would move to low risk if debt reduction continued from operating cash flow without secured debt issuance, and to high risk if debt-funded acquisitions or a distribution were funded ahead of the unsecured and second lien notes, or if the proxy statement showed the family holding a controlling majority of votes.

Net debt over reported EBITDA was 4.90x at FY2024, 8.55x at FY2025 and 8.42x on the last twelve months, and 7.94x on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, because reported EBITDA fell 43.84% as political advertising fell 91.55%, so creditors carry the debt on off-year earnings until 2026 political revenue is booked. The pro forma figure after the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment is USD 5,675 million, or 8.48x; the figure after the 2026-07-21 repurchase is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is the thinnest dimension. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.84x at FY2024, 1.60x at FY2025 and 1.74x on the last twelve months, and adjusted EBITDA covered it 1.84x, so a repeat of the off-year trough would leave little room for a cost or revenue miss. Cash interest takes 12.23% of last-twelve-months revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is positive but small relative to the debt. Operating cash flow of USD 250 million less capital spending of USD 104 million gave USD 146 million over the last twelve months, and after USD 87 million of common and preferred dividends only USD 59 million remained, so deleveraging from internal cash flow is slow unless earnings rise. The FY2025 off-year left USD 96 million after the same items.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The maturity profile is the main support. No principal falls due before 2028, the USD 739 million term loan and the USD 750 million revolver are both due on 2028-12-01, and the USD 1,125 million of 2029 first lien notes follow, so USD 1,864 million, or 31.77% of principal, comes due by the end of 2029. Secured debt is 65.78% of principal, so the unsecured notes of USD 2,008 million rank behind a large secured layer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was USD 921 million, made of cash and revolver availability, before the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment and the July 2026 repurchase funded partly from the revolver, so cash after those events is not established. The receivables securitization of USD 400 million is fully drawn, so it adds no further funding, and the revolver amount drawn is not stated, so liquidity today is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 25, 33–34; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability depends on fee contracts and the election cycle. Retransmission consent and network affiliation economics set the cash margin, and political advertising swings earnings between even and odd years, so the 2027 off-year and the renewals of network agreements from mid-2027 to the end of 2028 are the periods in which refinancing and earnings pressures meet. Management guidance for the third quarter of 2026 points to revenue of USD 935 million to USD 965 million against USD 749 million a year earlier, which is guidance and not an outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and financial policy are mixed and add to the balance sheet risk. The earlier assessment rates sponsor and governance risk as medium because acquisitions were funded partly with first lien notes while dividends continued, and because a ten-vote share class concentrates voting power; the preferred stock repurchase at a discount and the debt repurchases are the countervailing actions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better view is that 2026 is an election year with political advertising already at USD 113 million in the first half against USD 22 million, and the company guides third quarter political revenue of USD 165 million to USD 185 million and the guided revenue implies growth of 24.83% to 28.84% over the prior-year quarter. If those results are met and the revolver balance proves small, last-twelve-months earnings would rise sharply and leverage would fall, and the issuer's covenant total net leverage of 5.73x already sits below its 7.00x incurrence level. The view would improve if reported results meet guidance and debt is reduced from cash flow, and worsen if third quarter revenue misses the low end of guidance, if the revolver is drawn further, or if affiliation renewals raise network fees faster than retransmission revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 37; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The financial profile rests on twelve-month figures that include a quarter in which acquired stations contributed only part of a period, so the leverage and cover ratios may overstate or understate the run rate of the enlarged group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ratings, market prices and peer benchmarks were not part of the evidence, so the view is an absolute fundamental assessment and says nothing about how the debt trades or compares with similar broadcasters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The tests that govern distributions, additional debt and liens are known only from filing summaries, so the downside path assumes management policy rather than testing what the documents would allow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market rank are a strength. The group reaches about 37% of US households and holds the top-rated station in 77 markets, with no market above 5% of revenue, so a local downturn or one lost advertiser does little to debt service and the stations keep bargaining power with distributors, which supports refinancing access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A back-ended maturity profile is a strength. No principal is due before 2028 and USD 1,864 million falls due by the end of 2029, so the company does not need the capital markets in the 2026 cycle, which lowers near-term default risk even though leverage is high.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A path to higher earnings in the current cycle is a strength. Political advertising of USD 113 million in the first half of 2026 and guided third quarter political revenue of USD 165 million to USD 185 million would lift twelve-month earnings and cover if realised, which gives management a credible route to deleveraging without asset sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage and cover on reported earnings are the main weakness. Net debt of 8.42x reported EBITDA (8.48x pro forma after the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment) and cover of 1.74x leave little tolerance for a miss, so a fall in earnings would raise leverage and squeeze free cash flow before any covenant is tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dependence on fee contracts and the cycle is a weakness. Retransmission consent revenue was 46.17% of FY2025 revenue and network fees took a large share of it, with political advertising 1.36% of revenue in the off-year, so earnings can fall by 43.84% between an election year and the following year and renewals can reset fees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy and secured-debt priority are a weakness. Acquisitions funded partly with first lien notes and maintained dividends raise secured debt ahead of the unsecured and second lien notes, and the family-influenced control structure means these choices are decided by shareholders, so recovery for junior creditors is more exposed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The revenue base is a large station group with two fee lines and one cyclical line. Core advertising of USD 1,452 million and retransmission consent revenue of USD 1,429 million supply 46.91% and 46.17% of FY2025 revenue, political advertising swings by even and odd years, and network affiliation fees of USD 882 million are the largest cost, so net retransmission revenue of USD 547 million is the margin that matters. Pricing power sits partly with the group, which negotiates retransmission with distributors, and partly with the networks that set affiliation fees at renewal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; calculation C15; calculation C17; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost flexibility is limited because network fees and station staffing are largely fixed in the short run, so earnings move more than revenue: reported EBITDA fell 43.84% when revenue fell 15.07% between FY2024 and FY2025. Capital intensity is modest, with USD 108 million of purchases of property and equipment in FY2025, which leaves operating cash flow available for interest, dividends and acquisitions, but conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow is low after USD 385 million of cash interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C14; calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 75

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is high: the four major networks set affiliation fees and the agreements expire between mid-2027 and the end of 2028, so renewals can move USD 882 million of annual cost. Buyer power rests with distributors: retransmission revenue fell in the first half of 2026 on subscriber declines, a station moving to independent status and a resolved dispute, so the largest fee line is under pressure. Entry barriers are real because broadcast licences are limited in each area and ownership rules cap national reach, but the same rules limit the group's ability to buy more stations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy and the economy matter through two channels. Advertising budgets follow the economy, and the election cycle supplies political revenue in even years, so regulation of ownership and the timing of pending station approvals affect growth plans that management has linked to expected ownership reform. These factors support a view that growth depends on regulators and the cycle rather than on organic share gains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwind is the 2026 election cycle, with first-half political advertising of USD 113 million and guided third quarter political revenue of USD 165 million to USD 185 million, and the headwinds are the 2027 off-year, subscriber declines and the maturity of the term loan and revolver on 2028-12-01. Over three to five years the outcome depends on whether network and distributor renewals leave net retransmission revenue intact and whether acquisitions add earnings that exceed their secured-debt cost, which is not disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A realistic downside starts with the 2027 off-year: political advertising reverts to the FY2025 level of USD 42 million, and retransmission revenue falls further as subscriber declines continue while network renewals begin. Revenue and reported EBITDA would then move toward the FY2025 outcome, when reported EBITDA of USD 629 million covered cash interest only 1.60x. Free cash flow after dividends was USD 96 million in that off-year, so the group avoids liquidity distress if it holds acquisitions and repurchases to cash flow, but a revolver-funded repurchase or purchase would reduce the USD 745 million of availability just as the term loan and revolver approach their 2028-12-01 maturity. Management levers are suspending the common dividend of USD 33 million, using the USD 250 million repurchase authorization more sparingly and delaying acquisitions; these are possible but not documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 75; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, GRAY MEDIA, INC presents an adequate business profile supported by top-ranked stations, diversified markets and a back-ended maturity profile, but credit quality is constrained by net debt of 8.42x reported EBITDA (8.48x pro forma after the 2026-07-01 acquisition payment), cover of 1.74x and secured debt of 65.78% of principal. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in election years and weak in off-years because political revenue and fee renewals drive earnings. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2026 election-year result, the revolver balance and renewals of network and distributor contracts. The primary downside path is an off-year earnings trough in 2027 that coincides with a drawn revolver ahead of the 2028-12-01 maturity. Further analysis would require the revolver balance after 2026-07-21, third quarter 2026 results, the executed debt documents and the proxy statement. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 maturities from a weak off-year earnings base with a drawn revolver.
